job.title: Finance Specialist
job.description:
ROLE DETAILS
  • Up to $105,000 + super
  • Sydney CBD, fully office based
  • Permanent, full-time
ABOUT THE COMPANY
This is a high-growth fintech making financial life simpler for thousands of customers across Australia, New Zealand and the UK. The business is collaborative, data-informed and curious about using AI to work smarter. 

ABOUT THE ROLE
As the dedicated finance specialist for the Australian entity, you’ll keep the finances accurate, timely and well organised. Reporting to the Finance Manager, you’ll handle the day-to-day finance function, from AP and AR through to month-end, BAS and statutory reporting. You’ll be the go-to finance person in Sydney, partnering with department managers, external bookkeepers and advisors. This is a great step up for an assistant accountant ready to broaden their remit and improve processes.

DUTIES
  • Manage day-to-day AP, AR and oversight of external bookkeepers
  • Prepare monthly management accounts, budget variance analysis and key metric reports
  • Support GST, PAYG withholding, FBT, payroll tax and BAS lodgements
  • Assist with statutory financial statements alongside external auditors and advisors
  • Monitor bank accounts and support treasury, including intercompany cash allocation and term deposits
  • Partner with department managers and leadership on budgets, cash flow forecasts and projections
  • Help prepare payroll for the Australian entity
  • Drive process improvements and identify ways to automate routine tasks using AI
  • Contribute to right-sized financial policies as the business scales
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Degree in accounting, finance or a related field
  • Working towards or recently completed CA, CPA or ACCA
  • Experience as an assistant accountant or similar, with exposure to AP, AR, month-end and BAS
  • Confidence working autonomously, with regular check-ins from a remote manager
  • Strong communication skills and a collaborative, easygoing approach
  • Openness to AI and automation, and comfort adopting new tools
  • Desirable: payroll exposure and experience working with external auditors or bookkeepers

We ask that all interested candidates please apply online and wait to hear from us. Rest assured, we respond to every applicant, regardless of the outcome, so you will not be left wondering.

job.description:

Lotus People is thrilled to partner with an exceptional FinTech start-up that is rapidly growing and transforming how businesses and individuals manage their finances.

Customers are at the heart of everything they do here and they're always on the lookout for motivated customer service superstars who thrive in a fast-paced environment and genuinely love helping people.

job.title: Collections Officer
job.description:
ROLE DETAILS
  • $40 per hour + super
  • Sydney CBD
  • Immediate start
  • Office-based role
  • Minimum 1-month contract with potential to extend
ABOUT THE COMPANY

Join a leading Australian financial services organisation with a strong reputation for delivering customer-focused lending solutions. Operating in a fast-paced and collaborative environment, this business is committed to helping customers navigate financial challenges while maintaining exceptional service standards. You'll be joining a supportive team that values accountability, resilience and professional development.

ABOUT THE ROLE

This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced Collections Officer to hit the ground running in a busy, high-volume environment. Reporting to the Collections Manager, you'll play a key role in supporting customers with overdue accounts, negotiating suitable repayment arrangements and contributing to overall collections performance. Working alongside an energetic and driven team, you'll be trusted to manage customer interactions with empathy and professionalism while achieving collection targets.

DUTIES
  • Conduct outbound calls to recover overdue payments
  • Negotiate and establish suitable repayment plans with customers
  • Manage inbound enquiries from customers in arrears
  • Send collections documentation and correspondence as required
  • Maintain accurate customer records and account notes
  • Investigate account information and assist with skip tracing activities where required
  • Build positive customer relationships while achieving collection outcomes
  • Work efficiently in a fast-paced, high-volume environment
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Skip tracing experience required.
  • Previous collections experience within a financial services or related environment
  • Strong negotiation, communication and conflict-resolution skills
  • Ability to manage high call volumes and work to targets
  • Excellent attention to detail and administrative skills
  • Strong problem-solving abilities and customer-focused approach
  • Ability to learn quickly and adapt to changing priorities
BENEFITS
  • Competitive hourly rate of $35-$40 per hour + super
  • Immediate start opportunity
  • Convenient Sydney CBD location
  • Gain experience with a well-established financial services organisation
  • Collaborative and supportive team environment
  • Potential contract extension for strong performers

job.title: Executive Director of Advocacy
job.description:
ROLE DETAILS
  • Location: Surry Hills, Sydney
  • Organisation: People with Disability Australia (PWDA)
  • Portfolio: Approximately $8 million
  • Reporting to: Chief Executive Officer
  • Travel: Interstate and international travel as required
ABOUT THE COMPANY
People with Disability Australia (PWDA) is a leading national disability rights and advocacy organisation, dedicated to advancing the rights, inclusion and equality of people with disability.
As a cross-disability representative organisation, PWDA champions the voices and lived experience of people with disability, influencing government policy and driving systemic reform. With strong national relationships, a collaborative leadership team and a renewed focus on culture and governance, PWDA is entering an exciting chapter of organisational growth and impact.

ABOUT THE ROLE
This is an exceptional opportunity to lead PWDA's national advocacy function and shape its next chapter of impact.
Reporting to the CEO, you will oversee an $8m portfolio spanning individual and systemic advocacy, bringing teams together, developing leadership capability and strengthening organisational culture.
As a key member of the Executive Leadership Team, you will influence national disability policy, drive operational excellence and benefit from supported opportunities to develop broader executive capability and deputise for the CEO.

DUTIES
  • Lead and unite PWDA's individual and systemic advocacy functions, creating greater collaboration, shared purpose and strategic alignment across national teams.
  • Build leadership capability, mentoring senior managers, empowering decision-making and fostering a culture of accountability, trust and continuous improvement.
  • Champion a positive, inclusive culture, balancing empathetic leadership with clear expectations, constructive communication and decisive action.
  • Shape team structures and operational performance, identifying opportunities to strengthen capability, improve processes and maximise the effectiveness of advocacy services.
  • Oversee an approximately $8m advocacy portfolio, ensuring financial sustainability, effective resource allocation, funding accountability and robust governance.
  • Drive meaningful systemic change, connecting individual advocacy experiences, member priorities and evidence-based policy development to influence national reform.
  • Guide strategic policy priorities, contributing to advocacy across the NDIS, Foundational Supports and emerging issues affecting people with disability.
  • Strengthen influential partnerships with government, funders, disability representative organisations and sector stakeholders to expand PWDA's reach and impact.
  • Represent PWDA nationally, contributing to public advocacy, policy discussions, government engagement and sector leadership.
  • Partner with the CEO and Board, supporting organisational strategy, sustainable growth and broader executive leadership development.
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
They are seeking an accomplished, values-driven executive who combines exceptional people leadership with strategic capability and a genuine commitment to advancing disability rights.

You will bring:
  • Significant senior leadership experience, with a demonstrated ability to build high-performing teams, lead organisational change and foster inclusive, collaborative cultures.
  • An empathetic yet decisive leadership approach, with the confidence to navigate complexity, empower others and establish clear accountability.
  • Strong financial and operational acumen, including budget management, workforce planning, risk, governance and organisational performance.
  • A genuine commitment to disability rights, underpinned by a disability-affirming, human rights-based approach and meaningful connection to the disability community.
  • Strategic judgement and influencing capability, with experience translating complex issues into practical organisational priorities and meaningful outcomes.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills, with the ability to establish credibility across government, community and sector environments.
  • An understanding of disability policy and advocacy, including the NDIS, systemic reform and the importance of member-led representation.
  • The ability to lead through change, navigating sensitive conversations, competing priorities and complex organisational dynamics with integrity and care.
  • A relevant tertiary qualification or equivalent executive leadership experience.
Lived experience of disability is strongly valued, as is demonstrated connection to and trust within the disability community. Experience across disability advocacy, government, representative organisations or the not-for-profit sector will be highly regarded. PWDA also welcomes leaders from other sectors who bring relevant transferable experience, strong values alignment and a genuine commitment to its mission.

BENEFITS
  • National leadership opportunity with significant scope to influence disability rights, public policy and systemic reform.
  • Meaningful executive responsibility, leading an approximately $8m advocacy portfolio and shaping the future of PWDA's national advocacy function.
  • Opportunity to drive positive transformation, strengthening team culture, leadership capability and organisational performance.
  • Supported executive development, with opportunities to deputise for the CEO and broaden strategic and organisational leadership experience.
  • High-profile stakeholder engagement, building relationships with government, policymakers and influential sector leaders.
  • Collaborative, values-led environment, joining an Executive Leadership Team committed to inclusion, strong governance and sustainable change.
  • Purpose and impact, contributing to a nationally recognised organisation championing the rights and leadership of people with disability.

job.description:

Lotus People are delighted to be partnering with a rapidly growing and innovative business operating within the life insurance and financial advice sector.

Having experienced significant growth over the past few years, this business provides a unique combination of licensing, technology and operational support to financial advice practices across Australia.

With a collaborative, energetic culture and a strong focus on innovation, they are passionate about empowering their people, embracing new technology and continuously improving the way they operate.

Based in a vibrant Surry Hills office, the team enjoys a supportive and social working environment, with regular team activities, wellness initiatives and opportunities for professional development.

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced Life Insurance Administration Manager to take ownership of a key operational function within the business.

Leading a small team across Australia and offshore, you will oversee the day-to-day life insurance administration function, ensuring workflows are managed effectively, service standards are met and the team is supported to perform at its best.
